title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization, rework threadpool & pinning
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: CPU-side work in the request path (serialization/deserialization, scheduler handoffs, and KV cache access) was contributing up to ~40% of end-to-end token latency for small-batch workloads on CPU-backed inference and was limiting throughput on co-located control-plane nodes. This PR reduces redundant serialization, simplifies and rebalances the request threadpool, and applies explicit core pinning (NUMA-aware) for hot worker threads. Changes are focused on the serving runtime request path and scheduler integration with continuous batching so we get lower p50/p95 latency and higher sustained throughput without changing model execution kernels. Summary of changes: single continuous description string; high level bullets below are in the same string to satisfy artifacts consumers. 1) Avoid intermediate JSON serialization for internal request->task handoff by introducing a binary in-memory envelope (RequestEnvelope) used by the local scheduler and threadpool. In practice this removes two copy/serialize passes for each request. 2) Replace the global worker threadpool with a NUMA-aware bounded worker pool: background IO threads, lightweight network-handling threads, and a separate pinned pool for CPU-heavy pre/post-processing (tokenization, detokenization, KV cache lookups). 3) Implement explicit CPU affinity/pinning for the pinned pool with heuristics: one pinned worker per logical core in chosen NUMA node(s) for high-priority lanes (interactive inference). 4) Make KV cache reads lock-free for the common fast path: introduce atomic pointer swapping and a read-copy-update pattern for cache metadata; writes still take a short mutex but at lower frequency. 5) Integrate request envelope into the continuous-batching scheduler so we can batch without extra copies and avoid in-place JSON changes. 6) Add observability: new telemetry for per-stage CPU time, threadpool queue depth, and KV cache hit/miss latencies to help customers tune autoscaling and batching. 7) Backwards-compatible config knobs for pinning (disabled by default on multi-tenant hosted tier), threadpool sizes, and KV cache mode. Results: microbenchmarks run on c6i-like instances and internal perf-lab for medium-size open models: p50 token latency -8% (best-effort lanes) to -18% (interactive pinned lanes); p95 latency -12% to -25%; sustained throughput +18% (best-effort) to +32% (pinned CPU lane) under comparable CPU budgets; CPU sys% dropped ~15% due to fewer copies and less mutex contention. Integration test fleet (staging) shows reduced tail latency during traffic spikes and reduced contention on control-plane nodes. Safety/Compatibility: All changes are guarded behind runtime flags and a new config section serve.cpu_request_path. No model format or network protocol changes. Hotfix plan and rollback are validated in the PR checklist.

release_notes: Reduced CPU-side request latency (p95 improved up to 25%) and increased throughput by up to 32% for pinned CPU lanes. Adds new runtime flags: serve.cpu_request_path.enable_pinning, serve.cpu_request_path.pinned_cores, and serve.cpu_request_path.kv_cache_mode.
review_comments: Evan Zhou: Can you quantify memory overhead of the RequestEnvelope? Priya: ~120 bytes per active request on average; negligible compared to payloads and reclaimed after response.
Marta Alvarez: Suggest adding a knob to disable pinning per-deployment. Priya: Added serve.cpu_request_path.enable_pinning and defaulted to false for hosted tier.
Jonah Reed: KV cache RCU sounds good but ensure we have metrics for stale reads. Priya: Added kv_cache_latency and kv_cache_stale_reads metric.
Evan Zhou: CI flake in perf harness - fixed by reducing test concurrency in perf test harness to avoid noisy neighbours.

notes: Drafted with perf-lab benchmarks and staged rollout plan: enable on staging fleet for 48h then ramp to dedicated and private customers. Backport candidate for 2.3 release.
changelog_section: Performance improvements: CPU request path optimizations, thread pinning, lock-free KV fast path, and observability for CPU stages.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for RequestEnvelope serialization, integration tests for continuous batcher + pinned pool, and perf harness scripts. Ran perf-lab 5x with controlled CPU budgets.
